title: RFK Jr. Declares Cyclospora Outbreak 'Under Control' as Cases Top 7,000 Nationwide
excerpt: HHS Secretary says source of the parasite outbreak has been identified and recalls implemented, even as the FDA investigation continues and case counts climb across 34 states.
body:
• HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. declared the multistate cyclospora outbreak "under control" on July 21, saying investigators have identified the source and companies have implemented recalls.
  • Taylor Farms de Mexico has been identified as the supplier of shredded iceberg lettuce linked to the outbreak, with 1,644 confirmed cases, 94 hospitalizations, and no deaths across five Midwest states.
  • The FDA revealed that an earlier positive laboratory test on Taylor Farms lettuce was a false positive, and no product samples have produced a confirmed positive result for the parasite.

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said on Tuesday that federal officials have brought the multistate cyclospora outbreak "under control," claiming investigators have identified the source of the parasitic illness that has sickened thousands across the country.

"We do have the outbreak under control," Kennedy said during a healthcare fraud briefing on July 21. "We have done extensive forensics, epidemiological forensics and we have identified the source of the outbreak. We, and the companies that are involved, have implemented a recall."

A Growing Outbreak by the Numbers

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has identified nearly 7,000 cases of domestically acquired cyclosporiasis this season, including 1,645 confirmed cases and approximately 5,100 others still undergoing analysis. Of those, 1,644 cases have been linked to a specific multistate outbreak centered in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and West Virginia.

https://x.com/cspan/status/2079648990094569521

Michigan alone has reported 6,571 cases during the investigation timeframe, while Ohio has logged at least 1,244, Indiana 511, West Virginia 195, and Kentucky 192. At least 94 people have been hospitalized in connection with the outbreak. No deaths have been reported.

The outbreak is likely the largest cyclospora event in U.S. history, surpassing the previous record of approximately 1,500 cases linked to contaminated raspberries. If all suspected cases are confirmed, it could become the largest foodborne illness outbreak since federal tracking began.

Taylor Farms Lettuce at the Center

Federal investigators traced the outbreak to shredded iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms de Mexico to Taco Bell restaurants in the affected states. Michigan health officials said they completed more than 2,000 interviews with sick individuals, finding "very strong" evidence linking the illness to a single product.

"We have done extensive forensics, epidemiological forensics and we have identified the source of the outbreak. We, and the companies that are involved, have implemented a recall."

— Robert F. Kennedy Jr., HHS Secretary

Taylor Fresh Foods voluntarily recalled iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico on July 17, after investigators linked the product to Taco Bell locations where many sick customers had eaten. The recall covered lettuce shipped to 27 states, including shipments to Walmart and Jack in the Box, but did not include Taylor Farms-branded retail salad products.

Taco Bell said Friday that it removed Taylor Farms lettuce from its restaurants and its nationwide supply chain.

False Positive Complicates Investigation

In a significant twist, the FDA revealed on July 19 that an earlier laboratory result indicating a Taylor Farms lettuce sample tested positive for cyclospora was actually a false positive. "Due to the complexity in detection of Cyclospora, FDA laboratory experts re-reviewed the sample results and have concluded that the finding does not represent true amplification," the agency said.

No product samples connected to the investigation have produced a confirmed positive result for the parasite. The FDA said it continues collecting and testing samples while working with Taylor Farms.

The White House pushed back against Taylor Farms after the company posted on social media claiming the FDA had offered a "mea culpa" following the false positive disclosure. A White House official told the New York Post that the claim was "actively pissing us off," and the post was subsequently taken down.

FoodNet Cuts Draw Scrutiny

Kennedy also rejected criticism that the administration's response was hampered by cuts to the Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network, known as FoodNet. Last year, federal health officials scaled back the program, which had tracked foodborne infections for decades, narrowing routine surveillance from eight pathogens to just two: Salmonella and E. coli. Cyclospora was among those dropped.

"We did cuts in the FoodNet program, but they were for redundant surveillance, and all the states will tell you that we're still doing forensics," Kennedy said, calling criticism of the response "invalid."

Food safety experts have expressed concern that reduced surveillance could hinder the ability to detect and track outbreaks. Kalmia Kniel, a professor of microbial food safety at the University of Delaware, told USA Today that the loss of FoodNet data could impair officials' ability to identify outbreak sources and stop transmission.

What Indian Americans Should Know

The CDC recommends that consumers avoid shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico served at Taco Bell locations in the five affected states. While the recall has removed products from shelves, cyclospora symptoms can take up to two weeks to appear after consuming contaminated food. Anyone experiencing prolonged watery diarrhea, cramping, nausea, or fatigue should consult a healthcare provider and mention potential cyclospora exposure. The parasite is treatable with antibiotics, but left untreated, symptoms can persist for weeks.
